newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast crudes flat, buyers watch Canada import.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast crudes flat, buyers watch Canada import.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices were unchanged early, with spot crudes steady and California buyers holding out on news of a large offer of Canadian light.
Buyers bid for a 500,000 barrel cargo of Koch Alberta -- a 34 API gravity grade -- slated for loading at Vancouver, British Columbia, in mid-November.
The Canadian seller declined to name bidders or their prices. He said the cargo price would be based on a calendar-month NYMEX-West Texas Intermediate basis.
The cargo was offered because testing last month on a major Canadian pipeline left extra reserves of light crude.
The news could widen bids for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, which one buyer saw falling lower than the $2.50 most refiners were asking for.
A major producer kept his offer at $2.10 off November WTI.
November WTI was unchanged from Tuesday at $25.40/25.50 a barrel.
Outright prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude prices stayed flat at $23/23.30 a barrel.
The discount for ANS crude remained $2.30 a barrel less November West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, rose with postings to 16.80/17.00 a barrel.
And prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude also tracked higher postings to $18.15/18.25 a barrel.
